authoritative_perturbation_test.method: src/t3_perturbation_real_embeddings.py — perturbs post-merge clustering-eligible edges (10% removed, 100 seeds), real MiniLM embeddings via subset matching; corrected statistical test (each transition vs. the distribution of individual seed ARIs, not the CI of the mean)
authoritative_perturbation_test.interpretation: Only the 2022->2024 transition is robustly more stable than 10%-edge-removal noise (p=0.03 primary, p=0.01 secondary); 2020->2022 and 2024->2026 are not distinguishable from noise by this test. A partial, not uniform, P5 result. Not an equivalent-magnitude comparison (perturbation removes 10% of edges; real growth adds 40-92%).

lambda_decision.note: lambda=0 was chosen after an earlier (TF-IDF-based, degenerate) perturbation analysis; that analysis is NOT the authoritative perturbation result above, and should be read as 'lambda=0 is an untuned default that happened not to be contradicted', not as a result that positively informed the choice.

labels.pilot_note: CORRECTED from an earlier, wrong 2/4: 0/4 in this pilot, after checking every claim in each cluster's full list rather than skimming the first several. Sample (n=4) is still too small for a reliable rate estimate; a full-scale run with a Wilson CI is the natural next step. The real finding from this pilot is a process lesson: faithfulness judging must check every available claim systematically (e.g. per-entity search), not read a partial list and judge from impression.

pilot_detail.label: Tensorial & Magnetic Atomic Cluster Expansion
pilot_detail.gloss: Extends the Atomic Cluster Expansion framework to represent vectorial and tensorial atomic properties—including magnetic moments and charge transfer—for building interatomic potentials that predict energies, forces, and torques.
pilot_detail.faithfulness_note: Directly supported by claims describing ACE generalized to scalar/vectorial/tensorial properties with magnetic moments and charges; no unsupported specifics asserted.

pilot_detail.label: Equivariant/Directional Message-Passing GNNs for Molecules
pilot_detail.gloss: Graph neural network architectures—directional and SE(3)/E(3)-equivariant message passing—for predicting molecular properties and DFT Hamiltonians, evaluated largely on QM9.
pilot_detail.faithfulness_note: CORRECTED: originally marked partial_overclaim because the QM9 claims were missed on first pass. Checking the full 44-claim list finds: 'The Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) achieves state-of-the-art performance on all QM9 regression targets...' and 'Across all QM9 properties, the MPNN reduces the mean absolute error by 30-70%...'. QM9 evaluation is directly supported. The word 'largely' is a mild, hard-to-verify quantifier (only 2 of 44 claims are QM9-specific; most others describe DFT-Hamiltonian prediction on graphene/MoS2), worth softening in a future pass, but this is not an over-claim of an unsupported fact.

pilot_detail.label: Machine Learning for Multiscale Computational Modeling (Survey)
pilot_detail.gloss: A survey-level cluster covering machine learning methods (neural networks, generative models, transfer/meta-learning) applied to multiscale computational modeling tasks such as fluid mechanics, materials microstructure, and manufacturing, along with associated challenges like data scarcity and limited extrapolation.
pilot_detail.faithfulness_note: Consistent with claims describing ML as a surrogate/accelerant in multiscale modeling, CNN-based materials microstructure estimation, and memory/computation-cost challenges of hierarchical and concurrent modeling.

pilot_detail.label: Differentiable Density Functional Theory (D4FT)
pilot_detail.gloss: Methods for a GPU-accelerated, automatically-differentiable SCF-DFT implementation (D4FT), including neural local scaling and stochastic optimization, compared against established DFT packages (GPAW, Psi4).
pilot_detail.faithfulness_note: CORRECTED: originally marked partial_overclaim because this specific claim was missed on first pass. Checking the full 12-claim list finds: 'D4FT scales to carbon clusters up to C180, achieving wall-clock runtimes an order of magnitude faster (~1100s for C180) than PySCF, GPAW, Psi4, and JAX-SCF.' The GPAW/Psi4 comparison is directly supported.

labels.full_scale_run: NOT YET DONE — pilot only (4/14 level-0 clusters, 2026 snapshot).

extrinsic.conclusion: NULL / UNINFORMATIVE RESULT: TF-IDF gives zero lexical similarity between natural-language questions and short technical target names for the large majority of targets, so neither system can retrieve them regardless of cost. This is a scorer limitation, not a finding about the hierarchy's usefulness. A denser embedding scorer is needed before this comparison is informative.
extrinsic.caveat: An earlier version of this script reported a positive-looking result (hierarchical beating flat at low cost) that was an artifact of non-deterministic Python set iteration order breaking ties among zero-similarity candidates — corrected here.
